privacy: Private VPS repository names, paths, SHAs, credentials and machine configuration are intentionally not persisted in this public Project Brain artifact.
summary: Pocket × Pirate game-domain integration is merged, and the production frontend topology is now source-verified: Firebase Hosting is the authentication/launch-ticket launcher, GitHub Pages serves the game/runtime, and the runtime connects onward to the configured backend. The remaining browser-to-VPS chain is still BLOCKED because the backend ingress is raw-IP/non-canonical, server/worker parity is incomplete, general-player admission remains QA-scoped, and live authenticated browser gameplay has not been proven.

runtimeEvidenceRefresh.vantagePoint: VPS automation against public ingress, not an external browser
runtimeEvidenceRefresh.version: SAT labels only: server/game 8.4.0, API 1.1; not contract parity
runtimeEvidenceRefresh.corsPreflight: SAT: HTTP 204 for Pirate state OPTIONS with Pages Origin and authorization request header
runtimeEvidenceRefresh.wssUpgrade: SAT: Open, unauthenticated; no gameplay messages verified
runtimeEvidenceRefresh.pirateStateWithoutSession: HTTP 401; authenticated handler and worker readiness UNKNOWN
runtimeEvidenceRefresh.privateReviewConclusion: Required server candidate remains unmerged and its worker source pin differs from the merged client line; retained local edits require reconciliation.
constraints: No runtime change or deployment performed
runtimeEvidenceRefresh.progressPolicy: Earlier informal 33 percent gate count is not measured implementation progress.
runtimeEvidenceRefresh.reproduce: Use authorized private access to query configured health/version, send Pages-origin OPTIONS and attempt unauthenticated WSS upgrade; dispose socket and record statuses only. Compare public PRs and private server recipe separately.

findings.fact: Available rollout evidence supports a QA-scoped production path, including a single approved QA identity / one-user launch-ticket allowlist. That does not satisfy a general-player online admission goal.
findings.resolution: Use the approved QA identity for P4 E2E. If the product goal is general-player multiplayer, perform a separate explicit admission rollout and verify that scope before marking it SAT.

findings.fact: Current source-level deployment contracts show Firebase Hosting as the authentication and launch-ticket launcher, while the game/runtime is served from GitHub Pages. The launcher hands an authenticated launch to the game origin, and the game runtime then uses the configured API/WSS backend.
findings.resolution: Treat Firebase-launcher and Pages-runtime as intentional frontend roles unless a separate frontend consolidation is approved. P0 must freeze the backend API/WSS ingress rather than merely collapse frontend hosts.

findings.fact: The public Pocket client calls POST /api/pirate/vitals/input and sends newer Pirate state operations such as tradeQuote/trade. The canonical reviewed VPS server source does not yet expose the full merged contract; the corresponding server implementation remains outside the canonical deployed source line.
findings.resolution: Promote one reviewed server candidate into the canonical server line, then pin the deployed binary/source version in Project Brain. Do not treat client CI as server endpoint proof.

findings.fact: The reviewed public Pirate worker used by the shipped Pocket artifact includes the required vitals/trade/economy operations. The reviewed private server release recipe is not pinned to that same worker source; source parity is therefore not guaranteed.
findings.resolution: Build the VPS worker bundle from the exact reviewed Pirate source used by the release, package centralWorker + economy engine together, and assert required ops before artifact publication.

findings.fact: The production runtime and deployment contract still pin a raw-IP HTTPS/WSS backend origin. Firebase and GitHub Pages have intentional frontend roles, but the backend path still lacks one stable named ingress source of truth.
findings.resolution: Choose one stable named HTTPS backend origin and use it for apiBaseUrl, webSocketUrl, CSP connect-src, deployment verification and private ingress configuration. Do not treat the Firebase → Pages frontend handoff itself as the ingress defect.

findings.fact: The server-side Pirate worker must be explicitly bound at runtime. Repository review cannot prove the currently running VPS process has the reviewed worker executable/bundle paths and that the worker handshake is ready.
findings.resolution: Add a read-only readiness probe that reports worker contract/version/hash without secrets, and fail deployment if the worker is absent, stale or not ready.

findings.fact: Release evidence proves health/version, merged code, static deployment and behavioral tests, but no authenticated production browser gameplay transaction was completed.
findings.resolution: Run one QA-only Firebase launch-ticket flow in a real browser and verify REST + WSS + Pirate state + vitals input with redacted evidence.

findings.fact: The existing release verifier proves the configured backend health/version contract from automation. This is necessary but does not prove browser origin, auth, WSS, or Pirate gameplay routes.
findings.resolution: Keep this gate, but place it before dedicated browser-origin and gameplay-contract gates instead of treating it as end-to-end proof.

targetArchitecture.publicOrigin: One stable backend HTTPS/WSS hostname/tunnel origin
targetArchitecture.app: VPS application bound to loopback only
targetArchitecture.worker: Reviewed Pirate central worker pinned by source SHA + artifact SHA256
targetArchitecture.browser: Firebase launcher (auth + launch-ticket only) → authenticated handoff → GitHub Pages game/runtime → stable backend REST/WSS origin
targetArchitecture.authority: Pocket parent = session/validation/transport; Pirate/VPS server = canonical gameplay mutation

fixPlan.title: Freeze one backend ingress
fixPlan.gate: Firebase launcher and Pages runtime roles are explicit; apiBaseUrl/webSocketUrl, CSP, deployment verifier, Server.PublicUrl and reverse proxy/tunnel agree on one stable backend HTTPS/WSS origin.

fixPlan.title: Close server contract parity
fixPlan.gate: Canonical server source exposes Pirate state, vitals input, trade quote/execute and current worker ops; exact-head CI SAT.

fixPlan.title: Pin one worker artifact
fixPlan.gate: Server release manifest pins reviewed Pirate source + centralWorker/economy-engine hashes and rejects stale worker source.

fixPlan.title: Prove runtime readiness
fixPlan.gate: Public /api/health + /api/version + worker readiness + CORS preflight + WSS upgrade SAT from deployment automation.

fixPlan.title: Run real browser QA
fixPlan.gate: One approved QA identity completes Firebase launcher → launch-ticket → Pages → session → REST/WSS → Pirate state GET → vitals input → one idempotent gameplay operation SAT; this does not by itself prove general-player admission.

fixPlan.title: Promote authority
fixPlan.gate: Only proven scopes may be promoted. QA-authenticated live-host SAT must not overwrite general-player-admission VIOL/BLOCKED while admission remains QA-scoped.

doNotDo: Do not solve this by opening another raw VPS application port.
Do not use a rotating quick-tunnel URL as production runtime-config.
Do not merge client success and backend health into one PASS.
Do not enable broad player/economy writes merely to diagnose connectivity.
Do not persist private VPS repository metadata or credentials in public Project Brain.
Do not treat the intentional Firebase launcher → GitHub Pages runtime handoff as the backend-ingress defect.
Do not claim general-player multiplayer SAT from a one-user QA launch-ticket proof.
